messages:
maria: Heads-up — Security is asking us to enable VPC flow logs (ACCEPT) for the prod GPU subnets to meet audit minimums. Proposed change tomorrow 08:00 UTC. Any objections?
aj: Quick note: if we ship logs to CloudWatch with a CMK we'll see a lot of KMS decrypt/invoke QPS and CloudWatch ingestion costs. NAT egress could also increase if we don't use a VPC endpoint.
security-bot: SOC2 request link: https://okta.example/soc2-request — flow logs + 90d retention required for prod-enclaves.
kevin: Can we avoid CMK by using S3 delivery + SSE-S3 on the flow logs? That removes KMS QPS but adds S3 PUT costs and potential Athena/query costs later.
nora: We saw a weird side-effect last time we enabled dense logging: NAT conntrack fill caused GPU warm-pool attach delays. Warmup latencies spiked ~20s for queued provision requests. Risk to customer latency.
aj: Agreed. To reduce impact: sample traffic (10-25%), filter to ENIs tagged prod-gpu-*, and prefer S3 delivery via a privatelink endpoint to avoid NAT. Also batch/aggregate writes (max_aggregation_interval=600) to reduce write QPS.
maria: Draft terraform snippet below — intended to send ACCEPT logs to S3 with longer aggregation and a downstream sampler. Please eyeball.

```hcl
resource "aws_flow_log" "prod_gpu" {
  log_destination      = "arn:aws:s3:::redwood-prod-flow-logs"
  log_destination_type = "s3"
  traffic_type         = "ACCEPT"
  max_aggregation_interval = 600
  # note: AWS doesn't support sampling natively; we'll run a small lambda to drop based on ENI tags
}
```

kevin: Lambda sampler approach works but adds Lambda invocation costs and complexity. Alternative: use VPC Traffic Mirroring to a processing fleet — more infra but gives fine control. Both have tradeoffs.
finance: Ballpark costs: S3 PUTs + lifecycle -> infrequent retrieval ~ $3k-6k/mo depending on sample rate. If we accidentally route to CloudWatch+CMK add another $2k/mo. NAT egress worst case +$1.5k. Need sign-off for >$2k incremental spend.
sre: Operational mitigations: add a canary after flip that provisions a 5-GPU job repeatedly, watch conntrack, NAT gw metrics, and warm-pool attach latency. Add autoscale rule to bump warm-pool by +10 on deployment. Also add an alert on conntrack nearing 80%.
security: Compliance prefers CMK for auditability, but security will accept SSE-S3 if we can prove access controls and KMS for any downstream processing that needs decryption. If we do SSE-S3 we must restrict the S3 bucket to the logging role and block public access.
aj: Compromise proposal: enable ACCEPT-only flow logs to S3 with SSE-S3, put logs via VPC S3 Gateway Endpoint (privatelink where available) to avoid NAT, set sampling to 20% for first 72h, use max_aggregation_interval=600, run Lambda sampler to filter non-gpu ENIs, and revert sampling after verification. Monitor costs and warmup.
maria: Sounds good. Plan: sample 20% for 72h, SSE-S3, route via privatelink endpoint, canary + automated rollback window 2h. I'll post runbook and schedule. :thumbsup:
ops-bot: Change scheduled by @maria for 2024-05-10T08:00:00Z. Approval required from finance and security.
kevin: ACK — I'll own rollback if GPU warmup or conntrack spikes.
security: Approved contingent on bucket policy + IAM role scoping + post-deploy audit log review.
finance: Approved for a 30 day trial at expected cost <= $5k. Escalate if exceeds.
maria: Thanks everyone — I'll update runbook with exact playbook, rollback steps, metrics to watch (conntrack, warm-pool attach, nat gw bytes, S3 PUT QPS, KMS calls if any).
